name: Pellava Guava-Miso Spritz
description: Tessara's experiment in umami-forward soft drinks — a guava-forward sparkling water with a subtle shiro miso ferment note that arrives late on the palate. Launched to mixed reviews but found a devoted following in Tier 3 food culture circles.
flavor_profile: Bright tropical guava opens fresh and light; mid-palate introduces a faint savory, fermented miso warmth that shouldn't work but does; finish is clean with a lingering sweetness
cultural_context: Pellava is a conversation-starter drink — people either love the umami note or hate it, which makes it a social litmus test in Tier 3 dining culture; food influencers on the M88 mesh have made it a recurring topic, which Tessara exploits shamelessly in marketing.
story_hooks: Tessara quietly discontinued the real miso ferment in the latest production run and replaced it with a synth analog — food chemistry enthusiasts have noticed, and a mesh campaign is building calling for a boycott.

A Tier 3 restaurant sommelier claims that Pellava, paired with a specific synth-protein preparation, produces a flavor compound not found in either ingredient alone — and someone with serious money wants to know why.
The Tessara product developer who created Pellava's formula was let go and has since disappeared into the Shelf; a corporate retrieval team is looking for her, and she doesn't want to be found.
